subject.name_or_desc: An unnamed querent asking Lilly during the Civil War

context.question: Whether Sir William Waller or Sir Ralph Hopton should overcome?
context.asked_at: Friday 29 March 1644 (figure erected the day of the engagement)
context.setting: Friday 29 March 1644: Sir William Waller's Parliamentarian army and Sir Ralph Hopton's Royalist army were supposed engaged near Alresford, Hampshire (the Battle of Cheriton)

attachments.key_positions: Ascendant and Moon, Jupiter and Venus for Waller's side; Saturn lord of the 7th for Hopton; Moon in her exaltation with Jupiter; Sun, lord of Waller's substance/assistants, in the 10th in the very degree of his exaltation (19° Aries); only Mars and the South Node in the 9th (no supplies ready for Hopton); Saturn (Hopton's significator) sub radiis, in his fall, in no aspect to any planet, peregrine, aspecting the cusp of the 7th by square; Moon distant 11° from Venus, swift and increasing in light
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment (Fig. 20 in the 1852 edition).

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
